issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking an agent’s accounts of the full scope of the agent’s management is not confined to a particular transaction merely because the plaint identifies an amount received in that transaction.
material_facts: The agent was authorised to manage the principal’s affairs, including receiving money and investing it.
The plaint sought accounts of all transactions and amounts handled by the agent during the agency, as well as payment of any balance found due.
The principal did not know what the agent had done with the money, and the agent pleaded that some funds had been invested or otherwise dealt with on the principal’s behalf.
issues.conclusion: The suit was for accounts of the agent’s management as a whole, not merely for recovery of the amount identified in connection with one transaction; the High Court erred in treating that identified amount as the amount payable and requiring valuation on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: The nature of the relief is determined from the plaint as a whole. A demand for accounts covering an agent’s management is not limited to a stated receipt where the agent had authority to invest or otherwise deal with funds and the balance due cannot be known until accounts are taken.

rule.if: accounting_suit and agent_had_broad_management_authority and plaintiff_lacked_knowledge_of_management and accounts_of_all_agency_transactions_were_sought

predicates.accounting_suit: The proceeding seeks an accounting between a principal and an agent.
predicates.agent_had_broad_management_authority: The principal authorised the agent to manage affairs and to receive, invest, or otherwise deal with the principal’s money.
predicates.plaintiff_lacked_knowledge_of_management: The principal did not know how the agent had managed or dealt with the money.
predicates.accounts_of_all_agency_transactions_were: The principal sought accounts of all transactions undertaken by the agent during the agency, rather than an account of only one identified transaction.

issues.definition: When an accounting suit seeks accounts of all agency transactions and the principal lacks knowledge of management undertaken under broad authority, the suit is characterized as an accounting of the full management.

issues.legal_issue: In a suit for accounts, the plaintiff may use a tentative valuation, but it must be a genuine, fair, and reasonable estimate rather than a deliberate undervaluation.
material_facts: The principal could not know the balance due without an accounting of the agent’s management.
The plaintiff gave an estimate of the relief sought, and the Court found it adequate and reasonable in the circumstances.

The identified amount received in one transaction did not establish the amount ultimately due because the agent asserted that funds had been invested or otherwise dealt with on the principal’s behalf.
issues.conclusion: The estimate was adequate and reasonable and was not an under-estimate; the High Court was wrong to require valuation based on the amount it treated as payable.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 7(iv)(f) of the Court Fees Act, 1870, the fee in an accounts suit is computed according to the value stated for the relief. Section 35(1) of the Tamil Nadu Court Fees and Suits Valuation Act, 1955 likewise permits valuation on the amount estimated in the plaint. A plaintiff need not state the exact amount that will emerge from the accounts, but must make a genuine effort to provide an adequate and reasonable estimate and may not deliberately under-value the relief. The Court approved the principle stated in Chillakuru Chenchurami Reddy v. Kanupuru Chenchurami Reddy.

rule.if: accounting_suit and exact_amount_not_known_before_accounts and plaintiff_made_genuine_estimate and estimate_reasonable_in_circumstances

predicates.accounting_suit: The proceeding seeks an accounting between parties.
predicates.exact_amount_not_known_before_accounts: The amount ultimately due cannot be known until the accounts are taken.
predicates.plaintiff_made_genuine_estimate: The plaintiff made a genuine effort to estimate the value of the relief sought.
predicates.estimate_reasonable_in_circumstances: The estimate was fair and reasonable in light of the circumstances available to the plaintiff.

issues.definition: When an accounting suit seeks an amount that cannot be known before the accounts are taken and the plaintiff makes a genuine, reasonable estimate, the valuation is accepted as not undervalued.

issues.legal_issue: A court must reject a plaint for undervaluation if the relief is undervalued and the plaintiff fails to correct the valuation after being directed to do so.
material_facts: The dispute concerned valuation of a suit seeking accounts.
The Court stated that an accounts plaintiff need not know the exact amount resulting from the accounts, but cannot arbitrarily and deliberately undervalue the relief.
The Court found the valuation in this case adequate and reasonable, so it did not find the condition for rejection satisfied.
issues.conclusion: Order VII Rule 11(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure requires rejection of a plaint where the relief is undervalued and the plaintiff fails to correct the valuation within the time fixed by the court; that rule did not justify rejection on the facts of this case because the estimate was not inadequate or unreasonable.
issues.legal_principle: Order VII Rule 11(b) of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court to reject a plaint where the relief claimed is undervalued and the plaintiff, after being required to correct the valuation within the time fixed by the court, fails to do so. For a suit for accounts, the court must account for the plaintiff’s inability to state the exact result of the accounting and determine whether the estimate is adequate and reasonable.

predicates.accounting_suit: The proceeding seeks an accounting between parties.
predicates.relief_deliberately_or_arbitrarily_under: The plaintiff’s valuation is an arbitrary or deliberate under-estimate rather than a fair and reasonable estimate.
predicates.court_required_correction: The court directed the plaintiff to correct the undervaluation within a fixed time.
predicates.plaintiff_failed_to_correct_within_fixed: The plaintiff did not correct the valuation within the time fixed by the court.

issues.definition: When an accounting suit is arbitrarily or deliberately undervalued, the court directs correction, and the plaintiff does not correct it within the fixed time, the plaint is rejected for undervaluation.
